Spatiotemporal interaction specification

Source: R/spatiotemporal.R
spatiotemporal.Rd

A Knorr-Held (2000) space-time interaction for tulpa(): one latent value \(\delta_{st}\) per area and time, added to the linear predictor of every observation at that area and time. Pass the spec as tulpa(..., spatiotemporal = spatiotemporal(type = "IV")); it rides the nested-Laplace path beside the spatial and temporal main effects, with the interaction precision \(\tau\) integrated on the outer grid.

Usage

spatiotemporal(
  spatial = NULL,
  temporal = NULL,
  type = c("IV", "I", "II", "III", "iid", "separable"),
  tau_grid = NULL,
  shared = NULL
)

Arguments

spatial

The areal spatial spec whose graph structures the interaction (spatial_car(), spatial_bym2() or list(type = "icar", adjacency = W)). NULL (default) takes the fit's own spatial = spec. The interaction uses the graph's intrinsic CAR structure \(R_s = D - W\) whatever the main effect's family.

temporal

The temporal spec structuring the interaction in time, temporal_rw1() or temporal_rw2() (cyclic allowed). NULL (default) takes the fit's own temporal = spec.

type

Interaction type:

  • "I" (or "iid"): unstructured, \(R = I_T \otimes I_S\).

  • "II": each area its own temporal walk, \(R = R_t \otimes I_S\).

  • "III": each time its own spatial ICAR, \(R = I_T \otimes R_s\).

  • "IV" (or "separable"): \(R = R_t \otimes R_s\).

tau_grid

Optional outer-grid nodes for the interaction precision \(\tau\); the default is the engine's intrinsic-field precision axis.

shared

Not used.

Value

A tulpa_spatiotemporal spec.

Details

The interaction's prior is \(\delta \sim N(0, (\tau R)^-)\) conditioned on \(A \delta = 0\), where the rows of \(A\) span the null space of \(R\): for type II a walk's null space per area (its level, and its linear trend under an acyclic RW2), for type III a sum over each connected component of the graph at every time, for type IV both. These are hard linear constraints: the inner Newton solves on the constraint set and the Laplace approximation integrates over the \(ST - r\) dimensional subspace, with the log-density normalised by the generalized determinant \(|R|_+\). The interaction therefore carries no area level and no time level (and, under RW2, no area-specific trend) that the main effects already model.

The cells are laid out area-fastest: cell \((s, t)\) is coordinate \((t - 1) S + s\). A time whose rows all have an NA response is still a node of the walk, so the interaction forecasts it. spatiotemporal_effects() reads the posterior back per cell.

References

Knorr-Held, L. (2000). Bayesian modelling of inseparable space-time variation in disease risk. Statistics in Medicine, 19(17-18), 2555-2567.

Goicoa, T., Adin, A., Ugarte, M. D., & Hodges, J. S. (2018). In spatio-temporal disease mapping models, identifiability constraints affect PQL and INLA results. Stochastic Environmental Research and Risk Assessment, 32, 749-770.

See also

spatiotemporal_effects(), spatial_car(), temporal_rw1()

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
S <- 8; n_t <- 6
W <- matrix(0, S, S)
for (i in 1:(S - 1)) W[i, i + 1] <- W[i + 1, i] <- 1
d <- expand.grid(region = 1:S, year = 1:n_t)
d$y <- rpois(nrow(d), exp(1 + 0.3 * sin(d$region) + 0.1 * d$year))
fit <- tulpa(y ~ 1 + spatial(region), data = d, family = "poisson",
             spatial = list(type = "icar", adjacency = W),
             temporal = temporal_rw1("year"),
             spatiotemporal = spatiotemporal(type = "IV"),
             mode = "nested_laplace", control = list(progress = FALSE))
head(spatiotemporal_effects(fit, format = "summary"))
#> Spatiotemporal interaction posterior summary: 8 locations x 6 times
#>   s t         mean       q2.5          q50     q97.5        sd
#> 1 1 1 -0.148479588 -0.6176273 -0.105694509 0.1434200 0.1954687
#> 2 2 1 -0.128295811 -0.5207575 -0.092275053 0.1079577 0.1625603
#> 3 3 1 -0.081686523 -0.4010702 -0.053782120 0.1389099 0.1343069
#> 4 4 1 -0.006839270 -0.2556486 -0.004630852 0.2596565 0.1196976
#> 5 5 1  0.003773783 -0.2673289  0.003364371 0.2519359 0.1206082
#> 6 6 1  0.091613505 -0.1232738  0.060303019 0.4290250 0.1388464
# }
